answer: Each identity registers one jetty warehouse holding a kernel stock, posts a 70-credit bond, and pays a filing fee. Summit auditors publish receipt serials and recompute each stock against the public kernel-weight table; a shortfall, duplicate serial, or missing receipt burns the bond. The first filing costs 34 credits, the kth 34+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7027 and 1000 false identities pay 3,530,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds. A rented-stock ring fails because reused serials appear twice and both bonds burn. An honest operator pays 34 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
